Houston County, Georgia: Your Guide to Tax Sales

Looking to buy property at a discount? Tax sales in Houston County, Georgia, could be a smart move—especially if you’re after strong returns and stable long-term value.

Whether you’re just starting or already familiar with tax sales, this guide breaks it all down so you can get started with confidence.

Quick Overview: Houston County Tax Sales at a Glance

How the Tax Sale Works

  1. Check the Schedule – Auctions happen on the first Tuesday of each month. Dates may change for holidays, so be sure to confirm in advance.
  2. Register to Bid – Registration is required. Details and deadlines are posted in public notices and on the official tax sale page.
  3. Bring Certified Funds – If you win, full payment is due immediately, using a cashier’s check or similar certified payment method.
  4. Understand the Redemption Period – Property owners have 12 months to redeem the property by reimbursing you with a 20% premium (10% annually after the first year).
  5. Receive the Tax Deed – You’ll get a tax deed, but you must wait out the redemption period before taking possession or making changes to the property.

Real Estate Trends in Houston County

Houston County is more than just tax sales—it’s also one of the most affordable and stable housing markets in Georgia.

Why It Stands Out

  • Military Demand: Robins Air Force Base supports thousands of jobs and creates steady housing demand.
  • Affordable Prices: You get more space for your money compared to larger cities like Atlanta or Savannah.
  • Strong Rentals: Cities like Warner Robins and Centerville see strong rental demand and low vacancy rates.
  • Continued Growth: New neighborhoods and subdivisions are popping up in Perry, Kathleen, and surrounding areas

Pro Tips for Buying in Houston County

  • Double-check location restrictions near military bases like Robins Air Force Base.
  • Rural properties may require more repairs or cleanup but usually come with a lower price tag.
  • No access before sale—all property inspections must be from the street.
  • Don’t plan to move in or rent out the property until after the redemption period is over.

About Houston County

  • Population: Around 170,000 (2024 estimate)
  • Major Cities: Warner Robins, Perry, Centerville
  • Top Industries: Defense, healthcare, education, logistics
  • Local Perks: Access to parks, schools, shopping, healthcare, and family-friendly neighborhoods

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What is a tax deed sale?
A tax deed sale is when the county sells a property due to unpaid property taxes. The highest bidder gets a deed to the property, but the original owner can still redeem it for 12 months.

Can I inspect the property before the sale?
No, buyers can’t enter the property. You can only look from the outside.

What happens if the owner redeems the property?
You get back your investment plus a 20% premium for the first year or 10% per year after that.

Can I buy unsold properties later?
Yes. These are known as Over-the-Counter (OTC) properties. Contact the county for more details.

Do I have to live in Georgia to invest?
No. Investors from anywhere—even outside the U.S.—can participate.
